correctness.rationale: For a proper set \(D\), the complement of a complete multipartite graph is connected exactly when it is a singleton or meets at least two partite classes. Domination holds exactly when \(D\) meets at least two parts or is one whole part. The three excluded families used in the polynomial subtraction are disjoint, so the coefficient formula follows without inclusion-exclusion corrections. Exhaustive replay through order 10 matched the literal definition, the structural criterion, every polynomial coefficient, the published complete-multipartite minimum, and the published star polynomial.

value.rationale: The prior literature already singled out complete multipartite graphs at the scalar minimum level, and the polynomial itself was introduced as an object of study. The result closes the natural gap between those two strands by classifying every feasible subset and every coefficient for arbitrary part sizes. It also gives an exact total count and uniformly recovers known complete-graph and star behavior, making the result useful for coefficient questions and polynomial equivalence rather than only minimum optimization.
